_meta.title: GA4 Ecommerce Data-Layer Reference Schema
_meta.purpose: A complete, platform-agnostic specification for the dataLayer.push payloads a site should emit for GA4 ecommerce. Hand this to a front-end developer and the measurement is unambiguous.
conventions: Every ecommerce event clears the previous ecommerce object first with: dataLayer.push({ ecommerce: null }); — this prevents item arrays from bleeding between events.
currency is ISO-4217 (e.g. USD, INR). value is a NUMBER, not a string.
items[] is item-scoped: parameters set inside an item override event-level ones for that item only.
transaction_id must be unique and stable per order so GA4 can de-duplicate purchases on refresh/back-button.

consent._note: Pushed BEFORE any tag fires. 'default' runs on every page pre-interaction; 'update' runs after the CMP returns a choice.

view_item._note: Fires when a product/offer detail is viewed.

add_to_cart._note: Fires on add-to-cart. quantity reflects the amount added, not total cart quantity.

begin_checkout._note: Fires when checkout starts. value is the cart subtotal pre-shipping/tax unless your model differs.

add_payment_info._note: Fires when a valid payment method is supplied. payment_type is free-text (card, wallet, upi, etc.).

purchase._note: Fires once on order confirmation. transaction_id is REQUIRED and must be unique. value should equal item total + tax + shipping - discount, matching what the business counts as revenue.

refund._note: Full refund: pass transaction_id only. Partial refund: also pass the items[] being refunded. Enables revenue net of refunds in GA4/BigQuery.
